subject.title: Timeout compaction can report success but leave Codex channel session unrecoverable

question: When repeated timeout compactions still leave a Codex-backed channel session unsafe, should OpenClaw automatically roll over/reset the persisted session or stop with an explicit user-facing recovery action?
rationale: This choice determines how much channel history OpenClaw may discard or fork and how it avoids replaying tool/message side effects, so source inspection cannot safely decide it without maintainer product intent.

options.title: Automatic bounded rollover
options.body: After the retry cap, roll over the affected Codex channel session with side-effect guards, preserve the old transcript for audit, and notify the user that the session was recovered.

options.title: Explicit recovery action
options.body: Stop the turn with a precise message and expose an in-product Doctor/Fix or command action that resets only the affected session after user confirmation.

options.title: Fail closed only
options.body: Keep the current timeout failure behavior and document manual recovery, accepting that non-technical users may remain blocked without support.

recommendation.title: Automatic bounded rollover
recommendation.body: After the retry cap, roll over the affected Codex channel session with side-effect guards, preserve the old transcript for audit, and notify the user that the session was recovered.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent Codex compaction ownership work is closest to the native/app-server boundary that would need the recovery policy.
